focusableWhenDisabled.notes: Keeps the button focusable while disabled; the documented loading-state pattern (disabled + focusableWhenDisabled + aria-labelledby so the changing label is announced).

nativeButton.notes: Set false when render swaps in a non-button tag (e.g. <div>); Base UI then supplies role=button + keyboard handlers.

dataAttributes: data-disabled — present when the button is disabled

renderProp.elementForm: render={<div />} — Base UI clones it and merges its own props
renderProp.functionForm: render={(props, state) => <div {...props} />} — props are NOT auto-merged; spread them yourself
renderProp.merging: mergeProps (@base-ui/react/merge-props); event.preventBaseUIHandler() cancels Base UI's own handler

controlled.note: Button holds no value state and is neither controlled nor uncontrolled. Button.State = { disabled: boolean }. Interaction is native onClick.

formIntegration.submit: type="submit" must be set explicitly, otherwise the button will not submit.
formIntegration.disabled: A disabled button does not submit; with focusableWhenDisabled it stays in the tab order.

keyboard.keys: Native <button> semantics (Space/Enter activate; Enter submits when type="submit").
keyboard.focus: Native tab order; focusableWhenDisabled keeps disabled buttons focusable.

notableDifferences: React Aria's isDisabled becomes Base UI's native disabled.
No isPending equivalent — loading = disabled + focusableWhenDisabled (React Aria renders a spinner for isPending).
No onPress/press events — use the native onClick.
type="submit" is not implied; it must be passed explicitly.
Docs state Button must not be used for links (<a>): it enforces button semantics (role=button, keyboard, disabled). Style the anchor instead. React Aria has no such restriction baked into its Button.
Only state attribute is data-disabled — there is no data-pressed/data-hovered/data-focused set as in React Aria's render props.
